title.narrative: Nauru Acute Care Ward and Advisors

description.narrative: Procurement of medical advice and supplies to assist Nauru's medical system during the Pandemic and its immediate aftermath. This included fit out of a 17-bed acute ward at the RON Hospital and funding the WHO to carry out the STEPS Survey.

description.narrative: Australian Government funding to Beyond Essential Systems (BES) for Phases 3 and 4 of the Nauru Health Digitisation Project has facilitated health digitisation reform across the country in line with national priorities for public health, clinical services, and health supply chain. Over 2023-24, key achievements for continued digitisation of processes at the Hospital and Public Health include: digitisation of health promotion and food safety and environmental health reporting, roll out of software to the wellness centre and dental clinics, dashboards available for all public health programs, stocktake and data cleaning of the Hospital consumables store, as well as development of procurement guidelines and standard operating procedures. The Project has strengthened Nauru’s capacity to provide clinical care, increase meaningful use of data driven evidence-based public health action and response, and improved the quality and utility of communicable disease and NCD surveillance, improving health reporting across public health and clinical care.

INN869 Nauru Acute Ware & Advisors - procurement of specialised medical equipment and consumables to complete the fit-out of their recently renovated 17-bed acute ward. Procurement of Pandemic related advisors. ‍ INO107 Health Technical Support - implementation of the grant has gone particularly well due to having technical advisors work on the use of funds to ensure timely and effective use of funds against the priority areas. ‍ INO658 One health Companion Animal Program - AMRRIC team had a country visit and provided treatment to more that 480 animals, with 119 animals desexed. The team treated animals for common injuries and diseases, as well as providing anti-parasitic medications and vaccinations.
